item.title: Research Assistant – Applied Economics & Public Policy
item.description:
Note: Application deadline December 7, 2026. Start date January–February 2027. Salary $61,500–$65,500. Washington, DC (hybrid; option to work remotely twice a week including all Fridays). 0–2 years of full-time work experience required (internship experience counts). Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without immediate employer visa sponsorship; STEM OPT applicants need at least 2 years of remaining eligibility. Do NOT use AI to generate application materials. Apply via the application form linked in the posting.

Keybridge is a boutique economics and public policy consulting firm based in Washington, DC. For more than two decades, Keybridge has used expertise in applied economics, public policy, and data analytics to help clients anticipate and respond to economic trends and advance sound, data-driven public policies. Clients include leading trade associations, corporations, federal government agencies, and nonprofit organizations at the intersection of economics and public policy. Keybridge seeks a Research Assistant to apply quantitative and qualitative analytical skills to manage data, identify trends, estimate impacts, and evaluate the effectiveness of programs and policies. Washington, DC (hybrid). Salary $61,500–$65,500.

Key responsibilities include: cleaning, managing, and analyzing large datasets using Excel, R, and/or Python; conducting quantitative analysis (statistical analysis, composite index development, probabilistic modeling, ROI calculations) to identify trends, estimate impacts, and evaluate the effectiveness of programs and policies; conducting literature reviews and environmental scans to critically evaluate and synthesize existing research and build a credible, compelling base of evidence to inform policy development and client advocacy activities; designing and conducting surveys, interviews, and other data collection methods; drafting internal, client-facing, and public-facing products including memos, case studies, reports, data dashboards, and slide decks; developing subject matter expertise in areas including macroeconomic policy, energy and climate policy, innovation policy, financial policy, and public health; and providing project coordination support including organizing meetings, maintaining detailed notes, tracking task status, and facilitating client communications.

Qualifications: undergraduate degree in economics, public policy, public health, business, data analytics, political science, or related field; 0–2 years of full-time work experience (internship experience counts); strong written and verbal communication skills; strong organizational skills and ability to multi-task; work authorization that does not require immediate visa sponsorship (STEM OPT applicants need at least 2 years remaining). Preferred: professional experience with research, public policy analysis, or consulting; experience conducting quantitative and qualitative research; experience navigating key public datasets (Census, BEA GDP tables, BLS, EIA, FRED); experience with Excel, R, Python, or Tableau. Candidates are encouraged to apply even if they meet many but not all qualifications.

Compensation and logistics: salary $61,500–$65,500 plus annual performance raises, company-wide annual bonuses, and individual quarterly spot bonuses. Benefits include 401(k) with 4% employer match, 33+ days paid time off annually, paid parental leave, and 100% employer-paid platinum-rated health insurance. Washington, DC (hybrid; remote twice weekly including all Fridays). Start date January–February 2027. Application deadline December 7, 2026. Do not use AI to generate application materials.

item.title: Research Associate – Economic Studies (2-Year Program)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: 2-year Research Associate program. Salary $53,000–$62,000. Washington, DC (hybrid). Bachelor’s in economics, statistics, political science, or data science required. Proficiency with Excel required; experience with econometrics via Python, R, or Stata required. Must be currently authorized to work in the United States; no visa sponsorship. Submit CV/resume, two writing samples (research reports, working papers, peer-reviewed articles, data memos, blog posts, etc.) and optional cover letter as one PDF file. Apply via Cato’s careers portal. The Cato Institute is a libertarian public policy research organization.

The Cato Institute is a public policy research organization dedicated to the principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace. Cato seeks a Research Associate to support the R. Evan Scharf Chair for the Public Understanding of Economics in his research, communications, and administrative arenas. The Research Associate will help produce original policy analysis in multiple formats, support podcast production on The Economics of It, and have the opportunity to co-author work with team members. This role is available through Cato’s two-year Research Associate program, which offers educational sessions, networking, and mentorship from senior public policy scholars. Washington, DC (hybrid). Salary $53,000–$62,000.

Key responsibilities include: supporting the research of senior members of the economic studies team through literature reviews, summaries of new academic and working papers, and collating original datasets; collecting, cleaning, and analyzing economic and/or polling data and producing charts and data visualizations for publication; editing and fact-checking drafts of blog posts, op-eds, policy analyses, and books, verifying figures, quotations, and sources before publication; supporting the team’s economics podcast and video content by researching guests, drafting interview questions and briefing notes, editing transcripts, and tracking audience metrics; preparing scholars for events and media appearances by compiling supporting data and anticipating audience questions; monitoring new economic data releases, research, and news for timely hooks; and occasionally co-authoring policy analyses, working papers, peer-reviewed academic papers, and blog posts with team members.

Qualifications: bachelor’s degree in economics, statistics, political science, or data science; proficiency with Excel required; experience with econometrics via Python, R, or Stata required; strong organizational skills; strong writing and editing skills; experience and comfort finding, cleaning, and analyzing economic data from BLS, BEA, Census Bureau, and Federal Reserve; ability to explain economic research clearly to non-specialist audiences; and interest in libertarianism. Must be currently authorized to work in the United States; no visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary $53,000–$62,000. Cato benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, retirement contributions, generous paid leave, professional development support, and hybrid work schedule. Washington, DC (hybrid). 2-year Research Associate program. Apply via Cato careers portal with CV/resume and two writing samples in one PDF.

item.title: Energy & Environmental Policy Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: 2+ years of experience preferred. Salary $65,000–$85,000 depending on experience and quantitative skills. Fully onsite in Washington, DC (in-office position). Degree in economics, public policy, political science, or related field; statistics coursework preferred. Must be able to work legally in the United States; no visa sponsorship. Submit cover letter, resume, and a writing sample (fewer than 500 words describing an energy or environmental policy research topic of interest and why) via AAF’s JazzHR portal.

The American Action Forum (AAF) is a forward-looking, non-profit policy institute dedicated to keeping the United States strong, free, and prosperous, promoting common-sense, innovative, and solutions-based policies from a free-market, center-right perspective. AAF seeks an Energy & Environmental Policy Analyst to work with the Director of Energy & Environmental Policy to produce short research pieces on a variety of energy, climate, innovation, and environmental topics. The role produces original research and analysis of key energy-related policy proposals, legislative initiatives, and enacted laws. Washington, DC (fully onsite). Salary $65,000–$85,000.

Key responsibilities include: developing AAF’s energy policy research products including policy analyses, briefing papers, data-driven memos, and quantitative analyses; proactively pursuing research and locating data sources on a wide range of relevant policy questions in order to succinctly explain key policy issues; writing concise research papers and contributing data analysis to larger written products; supporting the Director of Energy & Environmental Policy with timely quantitative analysis and background memos; and working as part of AAF’s larger policy team.

Qualifications: degree in economics, public policy, political science, or related field (statistics coursework preferred); broad working knowledge of key energy policy issues; strong research skills and expertise working with various research databases or statistical packages (R or Python preferred); excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to multi-task and shift priorities efficiently; and an interest in working for a think tank that emphasizes smaller government, sensible center-right policy solutions, and smart policy options. Must be authorized to work legally in the United States; no visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary $65,000–$85,000. AAF benefits including health coverage, paid time off, retirement savings plan, commuter and dependent care benefits, cell phone reimbursement, and gym membership. Fully onsite, Washington, DC. Submit cover letter, resume, and 500-word writing sample on an energy/environmental policy topic via AAF’s JazzHR portal.

item.company: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), OMB – Executive Office of the President
item.title: Economist (GS-11/12/13/14) – OIRA, Office of Management & Budget
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: GS-11/12/13/14 grade levels available depending on qualifications. Direct Hire Authority — veterans’ preference and traditional rating/ranking do not apply; all minimally qualified applicants are forwarded to the selecting official. Transcripts required at time of application. Salary at GS-11/12/13/14 locality pay for Washington, DC (confirm via USAJOBS/OMB). U.S. citizenship required. Drug testing required. Security clearance required (interim and/or final). Time-in-grade requirements apply for current federal employees. Excepted Service (at-will employment; not eligible for MSPB appeals). No relocation reimbursement. Apply via USAJOBS (search OIRA Economist Direct Hire).

The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), within the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) in the Executive Office of the President, seeks Economists to join its team. OIRA is the federal government’s central office for reviewing significant federal regulations and information collection under the Paperwork Reduction Act, ensuring that government regulations and information policy regarding banking, capital and financial markets, tax policy, education, income maintenance, labor, and related sectors are effective, efficient, informed by quality analysis, in the public interest, and consistent with Administration priorities. Washington, DC. Salary at GS-11/12/13/14 locality pay.

Key responsibilities include: engaging primarily in regulatory impact analysis review and analysis within the branch, including reviewing agency regulatory analyses for consistency with cost-benefit analysis principles and official OMB guidance and policy; coordinating and reviewing regulatory analysis of actions submitted to OIRA under Executive Orders 12866, 14192, and 14215; examining the economic consequences of regulatory activities related to banking, tax policy/administration, capital markets, financial services, education, income maintenance, and labor; working on a range of policymaking issues and participating in cross-cutting research studies with other OIRA staff, divisions of OMB, EOP offices, and Federal agencies; reviewing current economic and technical literature for relevant concepts, data, and conclusions; assessing the strengths and weaknesses of statistical methods and procedures in federal government surveys and information collections; and providing advice on the advantages and disadvantages of various data science approaches.

Qualifications: degree in economics including at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus (required for all grade levels). GS-11: 1 year specialized experience at GS-09 supporting cost-benefit or regulatory impact analyses, documenting analytical objectives, and communicating basic economic information; OR PhD or 3 full years of progressively higher graduate education; OR combination. GS-12: 1 year at GS-11 conducting or reviewing cost-benefit analyses and communicating economic information to diverse groups. GS-13: 1 year at GS-12 leading multi-disciplinary cost-benefit analyses and communicating complex economic information to senior leadership. GS-14: 1 year at GS-13 serving as expert authority on cost-benefit analyses and developing organizational analytical standards. U.S. citizenship required. Drug testing required. Security clearance required.

Compensation and logistics: salary at GS-11/12/13/14 locality pay (confirm via USAJOBS/OMB). Comprehensive federal benefits. Washington, DC. Excepted Service (at-will employment). No relocation reimbursement. Direct Hire Authority — veterans’ preference does not apply. Transcripts required. Apply via USAJOBS.

item.title: UAS Policy & Program Analyst – Homeland Security & Critical Infrastructure
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: IMPORTANT — This is a more experienced role requiring 3–5+ years of experience supporting homeland security, aviation security, emergency management, critical infrastructure protection, defense, or related mission areas. Salary not stated — confirm via Partner Forces. Location and work model not stated in posting — confirm with Partner Forces. Apply via Partner Forces (recruiting@partnerforces.com for accommodations).

Partner Forces is a management consulting firm helping homeland security organizations solve their most pressing and complex challenges. Partner Forces partners with government agencies and industry to strengthen national security and critical infrastructure through expertise in strategy, program management, stakeholder engagement, technology implementation, preparedness, and business transformation. Partner Forces seeks a UAS Policy & Program Analyst to support homeland security and critical infrastructure security initiatives focused on unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and emerging counter-UAS (C-UAS) mission areas. Salary not stated (confirm via Partner Forces).

Key responsibilities include: supporting UAS and C-UAS related policy, research, and operational initiatives; monitoring and analyzing emerging UAS threats, trends, technologies, and regulatory developments; supporting the development of reports, briefings, presentations, training materials, and stakeholder-facing products; assisting with coordination across government, industry, and critical infrastructure stakeholders; conducting research and analysis related to critical infrastructure security, public safety, and emerging threats; tracking developments related to FAA regulations, Remote ID, BVLOS frameworks, and evolving C-UAS authorities; supporting meetings, workshops, outreach efforts, and program coordination activities; and helping grow and mature Partner Forces’ UAS and security capabilities over time.

Qualifications: 3–5+ years of experience supporting homeland security, aviation security, emergency management, critical infrastructure protection, defense, or related mission areas; familiarity with the evolving UAS and C-UAS landscape; understanding of UAS policy and regulatory topics including FAA Part 107, Remote ID, or related frameworks; foundational understanding of C-UAS technologies and operational considerations; strong research, analytical, writing, and communication skills; ability to synthesize complex information into clear and actionable insights; and comfort operating in fast-paced, evolving client environments. Preferred: FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate; experience supporting DHS, CISA, FAA, DoD, or critical infrastructure security programs; experience supporting trainings, workshops, stakeholder engagement, or operational coordination.

Compensation and logistics: salary not stated (confirm via Partner Forces). Partner Forces benefits. Confirm location and work model with Partner Forces. Apply via Partner Forces careers.

item.title: Management Analyst – Central Office Division Support
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: Entry-level (PG 13 Non-exempt). Bachelor’s or equivalent required; 1 year of administratively responsible experience preferred. Salary not stated — confirm via ACPS HR (classified as PG 13). Charlottesville, VA area (confirm onsite vs hybrid via ACPS). Tyler Financial system experience preferred. Apply via ACPS careers portal.

Albemarle County Public Schools (ACPS) seeks a Management Analyst to perform complex professional and administrative work in support of the district’s Central Office. ACPS is committed to ending the predictive value of race, class, gender, and special capacities for children’s success through high-quality teaching and learning. The Management Analyst may be assigned specific program or project responsibility; work involves responsibility to research, collect data, analyze, and publish information, as well as administrative, operational, and organizational development activities. Charlottesville, VA area.

Key responsibilities include: identifying, researching, analyzing, and collecting information to create reports and documents; researching and evaluating existing and proposed administrative or operational policies, practices, and techniques, and recommending improvements; researching and writing monthly, annual, and special reports for the department head; assisting in the preparation of departmental budgets; consulting with officials of other divisions and departments on matters of mutual interest; supporting departmental/school purchasing and procurement processes; participating in committees, teams, and project groups; working independently and assuming responsibility for projects and programs; and self-managing deadlines. Must be knowledgeable of all aspects of financials for the department, understand budgets and finance for the department, and have functional knowledge of accounting terminology, methods, accounting principles, and purchasing practices.

Qualifications: graduation from an accredited four-year college or university (or equivalent combination); 1 year of experience of an administratively responsible nature; thorough knowledge of the principles, practices, and techniques of public or business administration; ability to plan, organize, and coordinate the work of others; ability to communicate complex ideas effectively both orally and in writing; ability to perform complex mathematical and statistical calculations; ability to maintain financial records and prepare reports and statements; and proficiency with procurement software and Microsoft Office suite (specifically Excel and Access). Tyler Financial system experience preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary at ACPS PG 13 Non-exempt pay scale (confirm via ACPS HR). ACPS benefits including health and dental coverage, retirement, flexible spending accounts, paid time off, and wellness program. Charlottesville, VA area. Apply via ACPS careers portal.

item.company: Virginia Community College System (VCCS) – System Office
item.title: Data Analyst (Policy Planning Specialist II) – Institutional Research & Regulatory Reporting
item.description:
Note: Application deadline November 30, 2026. Salary $70,000–$85,000. Chesterfield, VA (VCCS System Office; hybrid, 2–3 days/week in office required). Restricted classified position dependent on continuation of funding; 1-year probationary period required. SAS programming experience required. Contact: Patsy Rose, prose@vccs.edu. Apply via jobs.vccs.edu (posting CLS_4873P).

Virginia’s Community College System (VCCS) has a 50-year track record of educational excellence and innovation, with 23 colleges on 40 campuses throughout Virginia. VCCS seeks a Data Analyst (classified as Policy Planning Specialist II) for its System Office to provide analysis, data management, reporting, and quality-assurance for institutional research and systemwide regulatory reporting activities serving Virginia’s 23 community colleges. The position works independently to prepare, validate, maintain, and analyze student and institutional data used for federal, state, VCCS, and internal reporting. Chesterfield, VA (hybrid). Salary $70,000–$85,000.

Key responsibilities include: performing data extraction, transformation, validation, reconciliation, and analysis using SAS and other approved analytical tools; maintaining established reporting programs and data files; preparing recurring reports and validation materials; investigating data-quality issues and selecting appropriate reporting methodologies based on business rules and specialized knowledge of related VCCS, state, and federal policies; developing new SAS programs when needed; conducting quality-control reviews; communicating findings; producing data files and reports; and providing college and System Office technical support, advice, and guidance. This position contributes to continuity of agency operations using established data-management and technical structures, adhering to quality-assurance procedures, and building knowledge of VCCS reporting requirements, student data structures, and institutional research practices.

Qualifications (required): knowledge of data analysis, data management, institutional research, or related analytical disciplines; working knowledge of SAS programming including data-step programming, SQL, data manipulation, file processing, and basic programming logic; ability to independently exercise initiative in creating reports and presenting data; ability to extract, transform, combine, summarize, and validate data from multiple sources; ability to work with large administrative datasets and structured relational or longitudinal data; ability to follow established data definitions, business rules, cohort specifications, and reporting methodologies; ability to conduct data-quality reviews and identify missing, inconsistent, duplicate, or anomalous records; ability to prepare recurring reports and analytical files accurately and within established deadlines; and ability to communicate data findings and technical information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. Additional considerations: knowledge of higher education institutional research or regulatory reporting; familiarity with SCHEV, IPEDS, Perkins, National Student Clearinghouse, or similar education-related data; experience with SAS programming and recurring production reporting; and education in institutional research, education, public policy, statistics, data analytics, or related field.

Compensation and logistics: salary $70,000–$85,000. Competitive VCCS benefits including excellent benefits and opportunity for career development. Hybrid (2–3 days/week in-office), Chesterfield, VA (VCCS System Office). Restricted classified position; 1-year probationary period. Application deadline November 30, 2026. Apply via jobs.vccs.edu (CLS_4873P). Contact prose@vccs.edu with questions.

item.company: ITS America (Intelligent Transportation Society of America)
item.title: Coordinator, Policy Programs & Engagement – ITS America
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: 2–3 years of experience in committee or program administration, project coordination, stakeholder or member engagement, policy, communications, or related work required. Salary $70,000–$80,000. Washington, DC (hybrid). Apply by emailing cover letter and resume to Kevin O’Hare at kohare@itsa.org. A writing sample may be requested.

ITS America (Intelligent Transportation Society of America) is the leading membership organization for the intelligent transportation systems industry, bringing together public agencies, industry, and academia to shape policy and practical guidance around transportation technology and policy. ITS America seeks a Coordinator, Policy Programs & Engagement to serve as the operational engine behind ITS America’s member-led committee structure, managing the calendar, logistics, materials, and follow-through for Standing Advisory Committees, Working Groups, Task Forces, and Communities of Practice. Washington, DC (hybrid). Salary $70,000–$80,000.

Key responsibilities include (Committee Operations, Administration, and Planning, 45%): providing day-to-day administration for all member-led groups; managing the committee calendar and scheduling meetings; contributing to development of annual work plans and timelines; developing and distributing agendas, presentations, meeting minutes, and supporting materials; maintaining accurate rosters, voting member records, and distribution lists across Outlook, Teams, Salesforce, and MyITSA; supporting the voting member process including annual calls for interest and tracking attendance; and organizing and maintaining internal and external file-sharing platforms. (Meeting Facilitation and Member Engagement, 20%): facilitating in-person and virtual committee and working group meetings; serving as a key customer service lead for committee members; building and maintaining relationships with members and co-leaders; and gathering feedback on meeting formats and processes. (Problem Solving and Process Improvement, 15%): anticipating and resolving scheduling conflicts and communication breakdowns; tracking deliverables, milestones, and deadlines across all committees; and developing and refining templates, checklists, and standard processes. (Communications and Cross-Team Collaboration, 10%): coordinating with the Communications Team on release of committee deliverables; and assisting in drafting one-pagers, memos, fact sheets, and committee summaries. (Policy Team Support, 10%): participating in weekly Policy Team strategy meetings and supporting weekly member calls; researching and tracking emerging policy and technology trends related to committee priorities.

Qualifications: bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; 2–3 years of professional experience in committee or program administration, project coordination, stakeholder or member engagement, policy, communications, or related work; exceptional organizational skills with proven ability to manage multiple calendars, deadlines, and deliverables simultaneously; strong meeting facilitation skills; excellent interpersonal skills and track record of building trusted relationships; proactive problem-solving mindset; excellent written and verbal communication skills; and proficiency with Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Preferred: experience administering committees, councils, or volunteer-driven bodies; experience in a membership association, nonprofit, or government setting; familiarity with transportation, ITS, connected/automated vehicles, or digital infrastructure topics. Up to 5% travel.

Compensation and logistics: salary $70,000–$80,000. Full ITS America benefits. Washington, DC (hybrid). Up to 5% travel. Apply by emailing cover letter and resume to kohare@itsa.org.

item.title: Federal Financial Management Analyst – Grants, Budget & Reimbursable Agreements
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: 1–3 years of consulting experience supporting Federal clients in financial management required. Salary $74,000–$124,000. Must be able to obtain and maintain a Federal Public Trust; must be a U.S. citizen. Bachelor’s degree in accounting or related field required. Must reside within 50 miles of DC metro area. Hybrid (2–5 days onsite at client’s or Guidehouse office). No visa sponsorship. Apply via Guidehouse careers.

Guidehouse seeks a Federal Financial Management Analyst to support Federal clients across the full spectrum of financial management, including federal grants, reimbursable agreements, procurement processes, and budget formulation and execution. The role requires strong client relationship and presentation skills, analytical skills, knowledge of Federal financial management regulations and processes, and the ability to translate complex financial data into clear insights and recommendations for clients. Washington, DC area (hybrid). Salary $74,000–$124,000.

Key responsibilities include (Financial Management & Analysis): providing ongoing financial management support to Federal clients in accordance with applicable Federal financial management requirements; supporting the quantitative development of business case documentation including needs analyses and cost/benefit analyses; preparing, reviewing, and reconciling financial documents such as federal financial transaction data, reimbursable agreements, and grant-related financial records; and identifying opportunities for process improvement. (Client Delivery & Communication): developing clear deliverables including presentations, reports, analyses, and dashboards that synthesize complex financial information into actionable insights; facilitating client meetings and working sessions; communicating with client and internal stakeholders on project status, findings, and next steps; and explaining financial concepts to non-financial audiences. (Innovation & Problem Solving): performing research and analysis on applicable Federal regulations, policies, best practices, and public financial data sources including USASpending.gov to investigate financial transaction-level discrepancies; and recommending changes to processes, tools, or documentation. (Leadership & Teamwork): working as part of a team or independently while taking ownership of assigned tasks; following established methodologies and standard operating procedures; and assisting on large to mid-sized, moderately complex projects.

Qualifications: bachelor’s degree in accounting or related field; 1–3 years of consulting experience preferably supporting Federal clients in financial management-related engagements; experience with Federal financial management such as federal accounting, grants management, reimbursable agreements, procurement processes, or budget formulation and execution; knowledge of Federal financial management regulations and guidance (DATA Act, Treasury Financial Manual, FFMIA, OMB Circular A-123, Federal budget process); proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Google Workspace; U.S. citizenship; ability to obtain Public Trust clearance; must reside within 50 miles of DC metro area. Preferred: active relevant certifications (CGFM, PMP, CFA, CPA, or similar); experience with Federal financial systems; experience with Power Platform or Google automation logic.

Compensation and logistics: salary $74,000–$124,000. Comprehensive Guidehouse benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), disability, tuition reimbursement, and professional development. Hybrid (2–5 days onsite), DC metro area. Must reside within 50 miles of DC metro area. U.S. citizenship and Public Trust clearance required. Apply via Guidehouse careers.

item.title: Policy Analyst or Policy Manager – Startup & Innovation Policy
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: Title (Policy Analyst or Policy Manager) determined based on experience. Salary $72,000–$96,000. Washington, DC (hybrid; in-person Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays). Recent experience working for a policymaker is a plus. Apply by emailing cover letter and resume to careers@engine.is with ‘Policy Analyst’ or ‘Policy Manager’ in the subject line.

Engine is a nonprofit organization that researches, develops, and promotes policies that support the innovation economy and the startup ecosystem. Engine seeks a new member of its policy team to help formulate and advocate for pro-startup, pro-innovation policies across a wide range of issues including intellectual property, telecommunications, intermediary liability, and more. Washington, DC (hybrid). Salary $72,000–$96,000.

Key responsibilities include: working closely with Engine staff to develop strategy and shape Engine’s positions on a wide range of policy issues; monitoring and providing analysis of policy proposals and conversations at the state and federal levels that would impact the startup ecosystem; communicating Engine’s positions to policymakers and their staff, including through meetings, written regulatory comments, and statements; working with Engine’s grassroots team to find, engage, and educate startups on emerging policy issues; and representing Engine in public and in working with allies.

Qualifications: demonstrated interest in the intersection of policy and entrepreneurship; ability to work with lawmakers on both sides of the aisle; willingness and ability to develop expertise in new policy areas with limited direct guidance; self-starter; ability to write clearly and compellingly including in Engine’s weekly newsletters, blog posts, op-eds, social media posts, comments to federal agencies, letters to Congress, and research projects; and ability to work well with and coordinate large coalition groups with disparate interests. Preferred: recent experience working for a policymaker; experience working on policy issues relevant to the startup ecosystem including telecommunications and intellectual property; and political or startup/VC experience.

Compensation and logistics: salary $72,000–$96,000. Engine benefits including health and retirement. Washington, DC (hybrid; in-person Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays). Apply by emailing careers@engine.is with ‘Policy Analyst’ or ‘Policy Manager’ in the subject line.

item.company: Bull Moose Project / Bull Moose Institute
item.title: Policy & Government Affairs – Research, Advocacy & Capitol Hill Relations
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: 2+ years of applicable work experience on Capitol Hill or in government affairs preferred. Salary $65,000–$85,000 commensurate with experience. Washington, DC (hybrid). The Bull Moose Project is a populist-right policy and advocacy organization drawing on the Square Deal tradition of Theodore Roosevelt; the role requires enthusiastic support for the organization’s mission and worldview. In lieu of a cover letter, submit a brief (250–400 words) reflection on Theodore Roosevelt’s ‘The New Nationalism’ speech along with a résumé. Apply via the application form linked in the posting.

The Bull Moose Project is a policy and advocacy organization working to build the intellectual and institutional foundation for a new American century, drawing on the Square Deal tradition of Theodore Roosevelt. Its affiliated 501(c)(3), the Bull Moose Institute, conducts the research and educational work that supports that mission. The Bull Moose Project seeks a motivated individual to help develop the organization’s policy and government affairs work. This position reports directly to BMP’s President. Washington, DC (hybrid). Salary $65,000–$85,000.

Key responsibilities include: writing and contributing to a variety of written policy products including reports, memos, op-eds, and video scripts; conducting research and translating it into action-oriented, external products; analyzing and tracking legislation to provide recommendations on BMP’s strategy around public positions, sign-on letters, bill sponsorship, comments, and feedback on draft legislation; supporting and developing programming for programs and events including basic operations work, confirming speakers, and assisting principals with speaking engagements or video projects; growing and maintaining relationships with government, industry, non-profits, and other advocacy organizations; occasional on-camera appearances for short-form video content (<5%); and occasional travel outside DC for BMP events or key meetings (<5%).

Qualifications: high school diploma or equivalent required; bachelor’s degree in public policy, political science, economics, or related field highly preferred; 2+ years of applicable work experience on Capitol Hill or in government affairs (ideal); enthusiastic support for BMP’s mission and worldview (required); entrepreneurial and able to work on long-term projects with minimal oversight; highly refined writing and communication skills with demonstrable history of being regularly published (preferred); subject matter familiarity with one or more areas of BMP’s policy priorities; and self-starter orientation. Requires enthusiastic ideological alignment with the organization’s mission.

Compensation and logistics: salary $65,000–$85,000. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance and monthly commuter benefit. Washington, DC (hybrid). In lieu of cover letter, submit a 250–400 word reflection on Theodore Roosevelt’s ‘The New Nationalism’ speech. Apply via the application form linked in the posting.

item.company: Federal Transit Administration (FTA) – U.S. Department of Transportation
item.title: Community Planner (GS-12/13) – Capital Investment Grants (CIG), FTA
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: GS-12 and GS-13 positions available. Direct Hire Authority/SME will be used to fill this position. Degree in community planning or related field (urban affairs, architecture, landscape architecture, engineering, sociology, geography, economics, political science, or public administration) with at least 12 semester hours in the planning process, socioeconomic and physical elements of planning, urban and regional economic analysis, and development finance required. Transcripts required. U.S. citizenship or national required. Government travel card required (position involves travel). Background security investigation required. 1-year probationary period — employment may be terminated unless continued employment advances the public interest. Apply via USAJOBS (search FTA Community Planner CIG).

The Federal Transit Administration (FTA), within the U.S. Department of Transportation, seeks Community Planners for its Office of Capital Project Development focusing on the Capital Investment Grants (CIG) program, which funds major transit capital investments across the country. The Community Planner will provide policy direction and guidance on public transportation projects completing the CIG process to FTA Regional Offices and external audiences, and may contribute to policy development related to the CIG program. This is a transportation planning professional role requiring skills in managing transportation planning programs and effectively representing the agency to Federal, state, and local officials and the general public. Salary at GS-12/13 locality pay.

Key responsibilities include: serving as a resource on FTA procedures and guidance related to transportation planning and project development processes for major transit capital investments and Federal laws, regulations, Executive Orders, and directives; keeping current on emerging changes affecting FTA programs and projects and providing technical advice to stakeholders; developing regulations, position papers, and instructions related to community planning aspects of FTA programs; reviewing regulations, reports, procedures, and techniques pertaining to community planning matters and providing comments or recommendations; and supporting statewide and metropolitan technical planning analyses, systems planning, Federal environmental review process compliance, and management of major transit capital investment projects.

Qualifications: GS-12 — 1 year of experience equivalent to GS-11 including: planning, coordinating, or monitoring planning projects or studies or carrying out operating assignments; developing or evaluating transportation planning and program development processes at a local, regional, state, or national level; and developing reports or presentations for meetings or conferences. GS-13 — 1 year of experience equivalent to GS-12 including: planning, coordinating, or monitoring grants or planning projects; developing, evaluating, or overseeing transportation planning processes at a local, regional, state, or national level; serving as an organizational representative at public meetings and industry conferences; evaluating data to support transportation program requirements; negotiating resolutions to regulatory or project-level disputes; and coordinating with FTA officials, local transit authorities, or other transportation agencies. Degree in community planning or related field with 12 semester hours in specified course work required.

Compensation and logistics: salary at GS-12/13 locality pay (confirm via USAJOBS/FTA). Comprehensive federal benefits. Direct Hire Authority/SME used — veterans’ preference does not apply. 1-year probationary period. Government travel card required. Background security investigation required. Apply via USAJOBS.

item.company: The Pew Charitable Trusts – Public Health Data Improvement Project
item.title: Associate I, State Policy – Public Health Data Improvement Project
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: Generally 1 year of applicable experience required. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required. Salary $69,100–$77,200. Washington, DC (hybrid; core in-office days plus 4 telework ‘flex weeks’ per year). Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the country without visa sponsorship. Apply via Pew’s careers portal.

The Pew Charitable Trusts’ Public Health Data Improvement (PHDI) Project is a foundational component of Pew’s larger Public Health Data Strategy, which focuses on helping state public health agencies collect, analyze, and use high-quality data to better detect, prevent, and treat the nation’s costliest and deadliest diseases. Pew seeks an Associate I, State Policy to support the PHDI Project’s efforts to advance state action to improve the collection, analysis, and use of health data to prevent and respond to public health threats. Reports to a Senior Manager, Public Health Data Improvement. Washington, DC (hybrid). Salary $69,100–$77,200.

Key responsibilities include: conducting and summarizing jurisdiction-based policy research to inform the project’s state engagements; monitoring key activities of state legislatures and agencies related to public health data sharing; supporting the development of presentations, talking points, and written products to support internal and external communications about the project’s state engagements; assisting in planning, organizing, and implementing stakeholder meetings and other events in partner states and at Pew; identifying and attending webinars, trainings, and conferences to expand subject matter knowledge regarding public health data sharing and state policy; and participating in activities that support project and Pew-wide objectives.

Qualifications: experience contributing to a team working on complex projects and achieving measurable results; aptitude to apply a non-partisan, evidence-based approach to projects and campaigns that require support across the political spectrum; excellent applied research and analytical skills including synthesizing large sets of information and identifying key themes; demonstrated time and project management skills including a capacity to meet multiple deadlines; bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; and generally 1 year of applicable experience. Preferred: skilled at developing and managing productive and collaborative relationships; experience with database and online policy research applications; familiarity with public health informatics, public health data, and data modernization initiatives; and experience working on policy change with or for government agencies (highly preferred). Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary $69,100–$77,200. Competitive Pew benefits including comprehensive health care, financial security insurance, retirement benefits, and work/life benefits. Washington, DC (hybrid; core in-office days plus 4 telework flex weeks annually). Occasional domestic travel. Apply via Pew’s careers portal.

item.company: Share Our Strength – No Kid Hungry
item.title: Manager, Local Government Relations – Mayors Alliance to End Childhood Hunger
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/2/2026.

Note: 3–5 years of relevant experience in local government, government relations, and/or public policy change required. Salary $71,000–$79,000. Preferably Washington, DC (hybrid) but could be fully remote for the right candidate outside the DC area. Up to 30% travel. This position may already be in the Batten Connect feed under a previous posting — check whether you have already applied before submitting again.

Share Our Strength leads the No Kid Hungry campaign, working to end childhood hunger in America by ensuring all children get the healthy food they need. Share Our Strength seeks a Manager of Local Government Relations to advance its mission to end childhood hunger and poverty by strengthening local government relations efforts. Working closely with the Senior Manager of Local Government Relations, the Manager will help lead the Mayors Alliance to End Childhood Hunger — a coalition of mayors dedicated to ending child hunger through shared best practices, policy advocacy, and community-driven solutions. Preferably Washington, DC (hybrid) or fully remote. Salary $71,000–$79,000.

Key responsibilities include (Mayors Alliance Management): managing day-to-day operations of the Mayors Alliance including onboarding new member mayors, producing newsletters and member communications, and planning virtual and in-person events and receptions; coordinating Mayors Alliance programming including Public Policy Council meetings, briefings, and sign-on letters; supporting recruitment and engagement strategies to grow Mayors Alliance membership; and contributing to the management of grant opportunities available to Mayors Alliance members. (Local Government Relations Strategy): supporting tracking and analysis of trends and elections affecting local elected officials; partnering with the Senior Manager to identify opportunities to influence policy implementation and drive systems change; collaborating with internal teams and external stakeholders; and supporting efforts to leverage relationships with mayors, city councilmembers, county commissioners, and other local officials to advance federal and state policy change. (Organizational Leadership): representing Share Our Strength to external audiences through conference presentations, community events, and meetings with policymakers.

Qualifications: bachelor’s degree in a related field preferred but not required; 3–5 years of relevant experience in local government, government relations, and/or public policy change; demonstrated experience working with local elected officials and government associations; interest in anti-hunger and anti-poverty issues; proven track record of building and managing effective and collaborative partnerships; excellent written and oral communication skills; demonstrated ability to initiate, organize, and prioritize multiple projects; and detail-oriented, well-organized, and collaborative. Up to 30% travel.

Compensation and logistics: salary $71,000–$79,000. Comprehensive benefits including health, dental, vision, retirement, wellness, and generous paid time off. Preferably Washington, DC (hybrid) or fully remote. Up to 30% travel. Apply via Share Our Strength / No Kid Hungry careers portal.

item.title: Market Development Analyst – Utility Regulatory Intelligence
item.description:
Note: Application deadline December 15, 2026. 2+ years of experience in the regulatory, utility, energy, or climate sectors required. Salary $74,000–$84,000 plus bonus. Location not specified — confirm remote/hybrid status via Uplight. Up to 5% travel.

Uplight makes software that manages energy resources in homes and businesses—including smart thermostats, EVs, solar panels, storage batteries, heat pumps, and consumer behavior—to balance the grid and accelerate the transition to clean energy. Uplight seeks a Market Development Analyst to turn utility regulatory developments into actionable policy and commercial intelligence, reviewing state utility commission dockets, filings, and legislation to identify budgets, program goals, policy mandates, and market developments relevant to Uplight and its utility partners. Salary $74,000–$84,000.

Key responsibilities include (Regulatory Intelligence): finding, monitoring, and reviewing state utility commission proceedings and relevant legislation across priority states; extracting critical information including program budgets, goals, timelines, policy requirements, and regulatory risks across customer engagement, energy efficiency, VPP, and DERMS solutions; combining AI and advanced research tools with independent analysis to deliver executive summaries and regulatory reviews for Market Development and other Uplight teams. (Commercial & Pipeline Enablement): equipping Sales and Account Management teams with utility-specific priorities, pain points, budgets, and regulatory context; supporting proposal teams with relevant regulatory intelligence; tracking filing dates, approval cycles, and program plans to identify potential sales opportunities before formal RFPs. (Advocacy & Knowledge Management): conducting research and developing supporting materials for senior team members preparing commission comments, testimony, meeting materials, and thought leadership; maintaining Market Development trackers, summaries, and shared resources; coordinating with Market Development, Sales, and other internal stakeholders.

Qualifications: 2+ years of experience in the regulatory, utility, energy, or climate sectors; familiarity with state utility commission proceedings and ability to navigate dockets and locate material information in filings; ability to distill complex regulatory and legislative materials into concise, useful written and verbal takeaways; strong research skills and comfort with data; organized and proactive approach to delivering timely work. Preferred: experience at a state utility commission or regulated utility; familiarity with VPPs, DERMS, or demand-side management; market development or regulatory affairs experience at a clean-tech SaaS company; background in economics or policy analysis related to demand-side management. No visa sponsorship. Up to 5% travel.

Compensation and logistics: salary $74,000–$84,000 plus bonus. Comprehensive benefits including flexible time off, generous parental leave, wellness stipend, 401(k) with generous employer match. Application deadline December 15, 2026. Apply via Uplight careers.

item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/1/2026.

Note: 1 year of professional-level experience in office or program management required, including conducting research/data analysis, maintaining accurate record-keeping systems, and managing financial operations such as fee assessments, billing, and revenue tracking. Bachelor’s degree required (or 2-year degree/60 credits + 2 additional years of experience totaling 3 years). Salary not stated — confirm via Anne Arundel County HR. Anne Arundel County, MD (onsite). Anne Arundel County Government seeks a Program Specialist I for the Bureau of Utility Operations to provide administrative and operational support to the utility allocations program, as well as assist with program management for other areas. The position requires a high degree of precision, consistency, and organizational rigor due to the direct impact utility allocation records and financial billing have on County operations and regulatory compliance. Anne Arundel County, MD (onsite). Salary at Anne Arundel County pay scale (confirm via HR).

Key responsibilities include: researching, evaluating, and updating permit allocations within the County’s permitting system including creating and revising allocation fees and Equivalent Dwelling Unit (EDU) counts; establishing, monitoring, and maintaining comprehensive electronic and paper-based records regarding water and sewer utility allocations; reviewing and calculating utility assessments, Capital Facility Capacity Charges (CFCCs), and billing data and coordinating with the Office of Inspections and Permits and Office of Finance to resolve errors; reviewing construction plans, permit details, billing data, and tax records for tenant improvements and developer projects to determine accurate EDU requirements; conducting monthly reviews of permitting, connection, and billing activity and generating and analyzing allocation reports; managing allocation reservation forms, coordinating fee schedules, preparing year-end adjustment schedules, and managing tax sale records; serving as county liaison for citizens, developers, and internal agencies regarding permitting and allocation inquiries; and assisting the Allocations Supervisor with daily operational management.

Qualifications: graduation from an accredited four-year college or university (or 2-year degree/60 credits + 2 additional years totaling 3 years of professional experience); 1+ year of professional-level experience in office or program management including research/data analysis, accurate record-keeping systems, and financial operations management (fee assessments, billing, revenue tracking). Preferred: prior government or public works experience. Supplemental questions required as part of application.

Compensation and logistics: salary at Anne Arundel County pay scale. Comprehensive benefits including medical/dental/vision, pension plan, deferred compensation, life insurance, 12 paid holidays, 13–26 days annual leave, 15 days disability leave, and 5 personal leave days. Anne Arundel County, MD (onsite). Supplemental questions required. Apply via Anne Arundel County jobs portal.

Key responsibilities include: serving as the first point of contact for visitors going to the House Gallery; operating check stands where prohibited items are collected and secured while customers visit the House Gallery; escorting large groups of visitors to and from the House Gallery; controlling access to the House Floor for staff conducting tours; enforcing access and decorum rules for House Floor tours; assisting with administrative tasks and organizational support for Chamber Support; and performing other duties as assigned.

item.title: Analyst Consultant – K-12 Education Resource Strategy (2027 Start)
item.description:
Note: Projected start date July 2027 or September 2027 (subject to business needs). Salary $75,000–$110,000 (starting salaries not at or near top of range). Watertown, MA office (hybrid, 3 days/week in-office required). Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. — no visa sponsorship including STEM OPT. R proficiency strongly preferred. Approximately 2–4 days of travel per month on average. Rolling recruitment; apply early.

Education Resource Strategies (ERS) is a national nonprofit consulting firm that empowers school system leaders to make transformative shifts in resources, structures, and practices so that all students—especially those with the greatest learning needs—attend a school where they can learn and thrive. ERS works with large public school districts across the country, with a focus on high-need populations. ERS seeks an Analyst Consultant to utilize proven quantitative analysis and logical reasoning skills to support systemic, transformative change in K-12 education via shifts in resource allocation. Watertown, MA (hybrid). Salary $75,000–$110,000.

Key responsibilities include: working in small, highly collaborative teams to help design strategic shifts in how K-12 state education agencies and school districts allocate resources (people, time, and money); breaking down complex, sometimes ambiguous questions into manageable components to inform actionable recommendations using methodologically sound quantitative methods; owning clearly defined workstreams and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment; supporting senior team members in developing recommendations that drive measurable impact for K-12 education partners; supporting research, data analysis, and modeling to generate insights and test hypotheses; and actively engaging in culture-building initiatives including quarterly ERS weeks.

Qualifications: bachelor’s degree emphasizing quantitative and analytical coursework with strong academic achievement; comfort working with numbers and data to break down and solve complex problems through quantitative analysis (efficiently and accurately categorize, make meaning of, and interpret large data sets with multiple variables); excellent verbal and written communication skills including the ability to synthesize complex material; AI proficiency — curiosity (required) and proficiency (strongly preferred) in using AI to augment research and data analysis; demonstrated passion for and commitment to ERS’ mission and values. Strongly preferred: proficiency in R including using it to clean, analyze, and interpret quantitative data. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship (no STEM OPT).

Compensation and logistics: salary $75,000–$110,000 (starting salaries below mid-range). Comprehensive ERS benefits including medical, dental, vision (100% covered), 401(k) with 3% match, parental leave, disability and life insurance, and generous PTO. Watertown, MA office (hybrid, 3 days/week in-office required). Start date July 2027 or September 2027. Travel approximately 2–4 days/month on average. Apply via ERS website.

The CDC Foundation seeks a Public Health Analyst to support the Overdose Response Strategy (ORS), an initiative funded by CDC and the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP) designed to enhance public health-public safety collaboration and strengthen efforts to reduce drug overdose deaths. The ORS PHA will support efforts of the Maine Office of Behavioral Health, Maine Information and Analysis Center (MIAC), New England HIDTA, and other key partners in the development and implementation of drug overdose information sharing systems and evidence-based prevention programs. Must be based in Maine. Salary $73,000–$89,000.

Key responsibilities include: facilitating data sharing and joint initiatives between public health and public safety agencies designed to address illicit drug use and overdose; collaborating with assigned Drug Intelligence Officer to build partnerships between local HIDTA program(s) and public health entities; identifying and promoting overdose prevention interventions at the intersection of public health and public safety; supporting and evaluating public safety-led interventions designed to connect people at risk of overdose to care and treatment; presenting to diverse audiences on overdose trends and local response efforts; and supporting projects that enhance public health/public safety collaborations through identification of appropriate local partners, qualitative and quantitative data collection, and dissemination of project findings. Additional responsibilities may include: conducting overdose and drug use data analyses; creating data visualizations; building partnerships with community members and partners; developing and conducting trainings on overdose prevention best practices; developing products such as briefs, bulletins, reports, and brochures; and supporting and evaluating public health and public safety interventions.

Qualifications: master’s degree in public health, social sciences, or related field + minimum 1 year of relevant experience; OR bachelor’s degree in public health, social sciences, or related field + minimum 3 years; OR associate’s degree + minimum 6 years; OR high school diploma + minimum 8 years of relevant experience. Professional experience or demonstrated interest in substance use disorder treatment, drug policy, and/or public health and public safety partnership. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Must be based in Maine. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

Compensation and logistics: salary $73,000–$89,000. Full suite of CDC Foundation benefits. Must be based in Maine. Hybrid (remote with weekly visits to MIAC Augusta, ME). Periodic in-state and out-of-state travel required. Relocation expenses not provided.

item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/24/2026.

Note: IMPORTANT — This is a more experienced role. Research or Data Analyst: master’s + 0 years OR bachelor’s + 2 years required. Senior Research/Data Analyst: master’s + 1 year OR bachelor’s + 3 years required. Salary $65,000–$85,000 commensurate with experience. Fully onsite in Washington, DC. Start date as soon as possible. Final title and salary based on qualifications. Stata, R, and Python required; SQL and geospatial analysis experience preferred. Finalists will be asked to pass an analytical assessment. Submit cover letter, resume, unofficial transcript, and writing sample at aei.org/jobs.

The AEI Housing Center is the nation’s leading market-oriented housing research center, operating at the intersection of data-driven housing knowledge and policy solutions. The Center seeks a full-time, in-person Research or Data Analyst (or Senior) to assist in creating, managing, and analyzing large datasets to derive insights and inform U.S. housing policy. Responsibilities encompass data science, business intelligence, and statistical programming. The position involves direct work with the Center’s co-directors on the full range of the Center’s initiatives. Washington, DC (fully onsite). Salary $65,000–$85,000.

Key responsibilities (Research or Data Analyst) include: performing statistical analysis and modeling according to detailed specifications to support small studies and fulfill ad hoc requests; combining processes, techniques, and methodologies from various fields to perform predictive and statistical analysis on large and often disparate datasets; creating data listings, tabulations, graphs, and figures for studies and reports; integrating data from various sources; assembling financial, workforce, economic, and statistical datasets to inform comparative and predictive analyses of housing issues; examining data for trends and anomalies to draw actionable conclusions; and forecasting trends and deriving key indicators. Senior level additionally: developing models, algorithms, and metrics to facilitate data interpretation; working with AEI employees to present and operationalize data; and independently solving a full range of complex problems.

Qualifications (required): Research or Data Analyst — master’s with 0 years of full-time experience OR bachelor’s + 2 years; Senior — master’s + 1 year OR bachelor’s + 3 years. Degree in economics, finance, real estate, public policy, computer science, or related discipline. Knowledge of Microsoft Excel. Fluency in Stata, R, and Python. Strong communication and organizational skills. Demonstrated interest in housing and public policy research. Strong understanding of statistical methods and data science techniques. Ability to manage multiple projects. (Desired): SQL experience (PostgreSQL, MySQL, DBT, DuckDB); geospatial analysis and visualization (Leaflet, Mapbox, ArcGIS/QGIS); web development (JavaScript, TypeScript); data visualization tools (Tableau, Quarto, ggplot2, Matplotlib); Git/GitHub and Docker. Finalists must pass an analytical assessment.

Compensation and logistics: salary $65,000–$85,000. Generous AEI benefits including 18 days paid leave, 12 days paid sick leave, paid family leave, medical and dental, HSA, FSA, tuition assistance up to $5,200, life and disability insurance at no cost, and 403(b) retirement plan with AEI contribution. Fully onsite, Washington, DC. Start date as soon as possible. Apply at aei.org/jobs with cover letter, resume, unofficial transcript, and writing sample.

item.title: Senior Research Assistant – The Hamilton Project (Preferred Start May–July 2027)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/24/2026.

Note: Preferred start date May 1–July 1, 2027 (future start). 1 year of relevant economics or policy research work experience required. Bachelor’s in Economics or related field required (master’s preferred). Salary not stated — confirm via Brookings; comparable to Brookings RA pay scales. Hybrid in Washington, DC. Unionized position (Brookings United / IFPTE Local 70). Submit resume, cover letter, writing sample, and unofficial undergraduate transcript via Brookings careers portal. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis; applicants contacted within 4–6 weeks if selected for an interview. Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.

The Hamilton Project (THP) at the Brookings Institution produces research and policy proposals on how to create a growing economy that benefits more Americans. THP focuses on a broad range of topics in macroeconomics and applied microeconomics with economic policy relevance including tax reform, social insurance, nutrition assistance, the labor market and AI, eldercare, early childhood and education, and healthcare. Brookings seeks a Senior Research Assistant to help develop and execute an overall policy agenda and policy strategy as a member of The Hamilton Project team, including doing original policy-relevant analysis and co-authoring research. Washington, DC (hybrid). Preferred start May 1–July 1, 2027.

Key responsibilities include (Research and Policy Development, 45%): with Director, Associate Director, and Hamilton Project staff, discussing and reviewing policy areas and ideas for research, development, and commissions; supporting policy development by researching various policy areas and remaining current on most recent writing and policy activity; independently analyzing data in Excel, Stata, R, or similar software and presenting findings accurately and accessibly both visually and in writing; and creating and/or maintaining charts, figures, and data interactives to illustrate research findings for internally authored and commissioned Hamilton Project papers. (Writing and Editing, 35%): co-authoring Hamilton Project research products including Economic Facts and long- and short-form empirical analyses on policy-relevant topics in economics; and developing and maintaining THP data dashboards. (Production Coordination, 20%): working with Director, Associate Director, and commissioned authors on policy proposal management including monitoring author progress, tracking paper drafts and timelines, and coordinating feedback; and on designated products, coordinating and/or executing quality control processes and liaising with communications staff on deliverables.

Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree in Economics or a related field (master’s preferred); 1 year of relevant economics or policy research work experience; strong quantitative and analytic skills as well as writing and editing skills including experience with Stata or R, Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; strong knowledge of and passion for public policy particularly domestic economic policy; must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.; and must be a team player able to work in a small, collaborative environment often at a fast pace.

Compensation and logistics: salary not stated (confirm via Brookings; comparable to Brookings RA pay scales). Comprehensive Brookings benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous time off, and workplace flexibility. Hybrid in Washington, DC. Unionized (Brookings United / IFPTE Local 70). Preferred start May 1–July 1, 2027. Submit resume, cover letter, writing sample, and unofficial undergraduate transcript via Brookings careers portal.

Cox. The Survey Center produces research on public opinion, social change, and political behavior including Dr. Cox’s bimonthly newsletter. Washington, DC (fully onsite). Salary $50,000–$54,000.

item.description:
Note: Application deadline February 1, 2027 at 9:00 PM ET. Apply at the FAO Schwarz Fellowship website (not Handshake). Eligibility: college seniors at accredited four-year colleges or universities at the time of application; eligible to work in the United States for the two-year fellowship duration. $50,000 year 1 (includes $2,000 start bonus), $55,000 year 2 (includes $3,000 end bonus). Philadelphia, PA. Hybrid (2 days office/coworking, 2 days school sites, 1 day remote; occasional evening/weekend events no more than once per quarter). Host organization: Children’s Literacy Initiative (CLI).

The FAO Schwarz Fellowship is an intensive, transformative two-year experience in the world of social impact, placing fellows at leading nonprofit organizations in Boston, New York City, and Philadelphia. The Fellowship pays $50,000 in year 1 and $55,000 in year 2 (with start and completion bonuses). The Children’s Literacy Initiative (CLI) in Philadelphia focuses on evidence-based and culturally sustaining literacy instruction to help all children learn to read and write by third grade. The 2027 Fellow will contribute to both direct-service work in schools and to CLI’s technology platform development. Philadelphia, PA.

Key responsibilities include (Direct Service, Year 1): conducting structured classroom observations documenting how evidence-based and culturally sustaining literacy practices are implemented; building relationships with educators, school leaders, instructional coaches, and families through school visits, interviews, coaching sessions, and family engagement experiences; identifying themes related to language, culture, identity, access, and literacy instruction; analyzing practitioner experiences to identify opportunities for organizational learning and innovation; facilitating educator and school-based learning exchanges that elevate community voice; and connecting field experiences to broader questions of educational equity, systems change, and organizational strategy. (Strategic Project): leading focus groups, documenting educator and family needs, and gathering feedback from early pilots of CLI Literacy Companion — a new platform CLI will design, test, and refine during the Fellowship; in year 2, taking a larger role in deciding improvements and expanding access; designing equity-centered prompts and content for AI-supported features; directing pilot implementation; and translating implementation findings into recommendations for long-term platform strategy.

Qualifications: college seniors at accredited four-year colleges or universities at time of application; eligible to work in the U.S. for the two-year fellowship duration. See FAO Schwarz Fellowship website for full ‘What We’re Looking For’ criteria.

Compensation and logistics: $50,000 year 1 (includes $2,000 start bonus), $55,000 year 2 (includes $3,000 end bonus). Philadelphia, PA. Hybrid (2 days office/coworking, 2 days school sites, 1 day remote). Fellowship begins summer 2027. Apply at faoschwarzfellowship.org by February 1, 2027 at 9:00 PM ET. Host organizations select applicants by end of April 2027.

item.title: Govern For America Fellowship – Matching Pathway 2027 (Government Roles, Multiple Locations)
item.description:
Note: Application opens December 14, 2026; deadline February 5, 2027. Apply as early as possible — applications reviewed on a rolling basis and review capacity is limited. Fellowship roles begin on or after June 21, 2027; mandatory in-person Summer Institute June 14–20, 2027. Salary $45,000–$75,000 depending on position and employer. Must be a U.S. citizen. Must have completed or be on track to earn an undergraduate degree by June 2027. Must be willing to consider opportunities in locations where GFA has identified need for emerging talent.

Govern For America (GFA) is a competitive two-year program that propels emerging leaders from diverse backgrounds into meaningful careers in government. Through the Matching Pathway, GFA connects candidates with eligible government roles aligned to their skills, interests, and career goals. Candidates do not need to have a role secured when they apply. Fellows work full time in government roles while participating in hands-on leadership development, dedicated mentorship, and a national community of peers committed to improving outcomes for communities across the country. Salary $45,000–$75,000.

Key responsibilities (depending on role) may include: working closely with government leaders on strategic initiatives and mission-critical priorities; conducting policy research and translating findings into actionable recommendations; analyzing programs, budgets, operations, legislation, or other government systems; using data and evidence to identify opportunities, improve programs, and strengthen outcomes; coordinating projects and supporting implementation of new initiatives; building and managing relationships with government agencies, community organizations, residents, and other stakeholders; and engaging communities and incorporating perspectives of people most impacted by government decisions.

In addition to their government role, Fellows receive: intensive leadership development; responsive mentorship; support from an extraordinary community of peers; regular professional development opportunities, peer learning, networking, and gatherings; coaching from experienced professionals; and access to GFA’s network of public policy experts, government leaders, Fellows, and alumni.

Potential locations include: Tucson, AZ; areas of California (Fresno, San Rafael, SF Mission, Oakland); Northern Denver; Norwalk and Stamford, CT; Wilmington, DE; Orlando, FL; Berea and Appalachian KY; Baltimore; Boston; St. Cloud and Northfield, MN; Akron and Dayton, OH; Tulsa; Portland, OR; Providence; Spartanburg, SC; Memphis/Shelby County, TN; select TX locations; Salt Lake City; Tacoma and Seattle; and Kenosha, Racine, and Milwaukee, WI. Available locations and roles may change.

Eligibility: U.S. citizen; completed undergraduate degree or on track by June 2027; available to begin Fellowship mid-to-late June 2027; willing to attend Summer Institute in person June 14–20, 2027; demonstrate passion for public service and desire to build a career in government; willing to consider government opportunities in cities and states where GFA has identified a need. Compensation and logistics: salary $45,000–$75,000. Financial support for relocation and emergencies on a case-by-case basis. Application opens December 14, 2026; deadline February 5, 2027. Apply at governforamerica.org.
