item.title: Senior Policy Advisor – Global Development
item.description:
Note: Application deadline November 19, 2026. Apply by sending a cover letter and resume to Info@FP4America.org with ‘Senior Policy Advisor for Global Development’ in the subject line. IMPORTANT — This is a senior role requiring a minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience. Salary $80,000–$110,000. Washington, DC. Demonstrated commitment to FP4A’s goal of increasing total U.S. foreign aid, with an emphasis on strengthening support for life-saving global health programs, is required. Experience in government or an aid implementing organization preferred.

Foreign Policy for America (FP4A) is a national organization advocating for principled U.S. leadership in the world, promoting sound policies, holding elected officials accountable for their votes and actions, and helping elect champions for their values. As FP4A enters 2027, it sees a critical window of opportunity to renew U.S. leadership in delivering life-saving foreign aid. The Senior Policy Advisor for Global Development will lead FP4A’s efforts to communicate that priority goal on behalf of the community to Members of Congress and their staff, presidential candidates and their advisors, and the broader public. Washington, DC. Salary $80,000–$110,000.

Key responsibilities include: developing and maintaining relationships with key offices on Capitol Hill as well as relevant executive branch officials as appropriate; closely tracking legislative activity related to priority issues including legislation, hearings, and floor debate; coordinating with external stakeholders including issue experts and representatives from allied organizations to develop and implement tactics to reach policymakers from educational events to lobbying; monitoring and responding to breaking news with a focus on portfolio issues including international events and executive branch actions; developing products that communicate detailed information about policy priorities including vote advisories, fact sheets, message guidance, press statements, and briefing materials; developing digital communications products including social media and website content that engage and motivate supporters to act around key policy goals; contributing to team-wide activities including the FP4A Leadership Summit and production of the biannual legislative scorecard; and contributing to strategic planning and fundraising.

Qualifications: minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience; familiarity with the legislative process including the appropriations process; demonstrated commitment to FP4A’s goal of increasing total U.S. foreign aid with an emphasis on strengthening support for life-saving global health programs; demonstrated understanding of and interest in foreign assistance and international development including global health policy (relevant experience in government or an aid implementing organization preferred but not required); outstanding written and oral communication skills; experience with coalition management and multi-stakeholder advocacy; and outstanding teamwork skills.

Compensation and logistics: salary $80,000–$110,000 commensurate with skills and experience. Highly competitive benefits package including fully covered health, dental, and vision insurance; 401(k) with match program; paid parental leave; unlimited paid time off; and more. Washington, DC. Apply by November 19, 2026 to Info@FP4America.org.

Note: Application deadline 5:00 PM ET, November 18, 2026. 3–5 years of relevant experience in policy research, analysis, or development required. Salary $82,000–$87,000. Fully remote with 10% travel for in-person team meetings and events. TSF focuses on state-based policy ideas grounded in founding ideals of political equality, universal rights, individual freedom, and economic opportunity. Comfort with high levels of ambiguity and a startup environment essential.

The States Forum (TSF) is a think tank-style organization that produces and disseminates state-based policy ideas through partnerships, policy accelerators, research, and convenings, working with policymakers across the country. TSF seeks a Policy Manager to support the development of TSF’s policy and idea products and manage the day-to-day operation of its fellows program. The Policy Manager reports to the Senior Director of Policy and serves as the main point of contact for the graduate student fellows program. Fully remote. Salary $82,000–$87,000.

Key responsibilities include: researching, drafting, and editing TSF policy products including policy documents, idea briefs, and memos that turn complex concepts into practical tools for state lawmakers and partners; managing the day-to-day operation of TSF’s fellows program from onboarding through tracking progress against TSF’s overall calendar; leading the internal process for idea briefs including review, quality control, and maintaining TSF’s library of ideas; conducting background research and landscape scans on policy topics; helping translate complex policy concepts into clear, practical products for state lawmakers and partners; supporting and onboarding new fellows and contributors; tracking contributor progress and alignment with the organization’s overall calendar; reviewing briefs submitted by fellows and contributors for quality, consistency, and alignment with TSF’s approach; monitoring state policy developments and legislative trends; and collaborating with the Senior Manager, Partnerships & Outreach to support dissemination of ideas through Substack posts, idea briefs, and event materials.

Qualifications: 3–5 years of relevant experience in policy research, analysis, or development ideally in policy, nonprofit, or government settings; excellent research, writing, and editing skills with the ability to make complex ideas clear and actionable; familiarity with state policy and the state legislative process (experience working with or for state lawmakers is a plus); capable of independently managing time and tasks associated with a fast-paced organization; and clear communication skills.

Compensation and logistics: salary $82,000–$87,000. Benefits including 75% paid coverage of medical and dental, unlimited PTO, 401(k) matching, annual professional development, wellness, and work-from-home stipends, and paid family leave. Fully remote with 10% travel. Apply by 5:00 PM ET November 18, 2026 with resume and cover letter.

Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions, advocating for public policies that enable competition and working alongside member companies to create economic opportunity, lower consumer costs, and bolster energy reliability and resilience. United seeks a Policy Associate to join its Virginia legislative team, driving legislation and supporting state-level campaigns that accelerate the deployment of clean energy projects and programs across the Commonwealth of Virginia. Must reside in or around Richmond, VA. Salary starting at $64,000. Start date November/December 2027.

Key responsibilities include: supporting the development and execution of state-level legislative and advocacy campaigns; conducting research on industry insights, state energy markets, political landscapes, policy developments, and key stakeholders to inform advocacy strategies and campaign priorities; building and maintaining relationships with policymakers, advocacy organizations, coalition partners, industry stakeholders, and regulatory staff; supporting engagement with decisionmakers and helping communicate United’s policy priorities clearly and professionally; using project management tools and internal systems to track progress, manage deliverables, and support both short- and long-term advocacy goals; maintaining organized records and documentation to support knowledge of United’s member companies, lawmakers, advocates, and other stakeholders; assisting in preparing updates, reports, and presentations on legislative progress, outcomes, and key metrics; and assisting with drafting regulatory comments in support of legislative implementation efforts.

Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; 0–3 years of professional experience, preferably in policy analysis, campaigns, and/or policy advocacy; a commitment to and track record of work that aligns with United’s Core Values; demonstrated ability to quickly learn and navigate technical subject matter; independent self-starter comfortable working in a remote environment; strong interpersonal skills; experience managing confidential information; excellent communication skills; and willingness to travel as needed outside Richmond (up to 15%). Must reside in or around Richmond, VA.

Compensation and logistics: salary starting at $64,000. Comprehensive Advanced Energy United benefits including remote work, flexible schedule, medical/dental/vision, FSA, profit sharing, $75/month wellness reimbursement, $100/month technology subsidy, accrued PTO, 11 federal holidays, annual end-of-year closure, 12 weeks parental leave, professional development reimbursement, 401(k) with matching, and WMATA Transit Smart Benefits. item.description:

Note: IMPORTANT — This is a senior role requiring 3+ years of successful grants management experience plus prior consulting or advisory experience. Salary not stated — confirm via EisnerAmper careers. Hybrid (up to 2 days/week at local office or client location required). Preferred location: Baton Rouge, LA (other EisnerAmper offices also considered). Ability to travel and work extended hours as needed. Grants-related certifications (CGMS, GPC, PMP, CPA) preferred.

EisnerAmper is one of the largest accounting, tax, and business advisory firms with approximately 500 partners and 5,000 employees across the world. EisnerAmper’s Government Services practice provides assurance, advisory, and outsourcing services to hundreds of governmental clients including federal, state, local, and county/parish governmental entities, municipalities, public retirement systems, school boards, and more. EisnerAmper seeks a Senior Consultant to support clients with monitoring state and federal grants including project eligibility, reporting, and recipient and subrecipient monitoring. Salary not stated (confirm via EisnerAmper careers).

Key responsibilities include: evaluating client needs and recommending project approaches and strategies; understanding and applying concepts from 2 CFR 200, executive orders, and OMB memoranda across the grant lifecycle; assisting in the review of funding requests and development of competitive grant applications; providing grants monitoring and oversight including recipient and subrecipient monitoring per 2 CFR 200; reviewing and analyzing grantee budgets for reasonableness and allowability of costs; supporting clients in navigating award terms, amendment requests, grant closeout, and compliance requirements; guiding clients through pre-award, post-award, and closeout phases; interpreting federal and state grant regulations including ARPA, BIA, DHHS, IHS, IIJA, and DHHS programs; preparing client deliverables; and providing specialized guidance to tribal, healthcare, and nonprofit clients in aligning funding opportunities with strategic goals.

Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree in Business, Accounting, Finance, Public Administration, or a related field; 3+ years of successful grants management experience; prior consulting or advisory experience; strong written and verbal communication skills; proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint; and ability to work in a fast-paced environment with multiple priorities. Preferred: experience working with state and local governments, tribal governments, healthcare organizations, and nonprofit entities; grant writing and application development experience; experience with ARPA, BIA, DHHS, IHS, IIJA, or EPA-funded programs; knowledge of federal compliance requirements and Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200); grants-related certifications (CGMS, GPC, PMP, CPA, etc.); and familiarity with AI systems (Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT).

Compensation and logistics: salary not stated (confirm via EisnerAmper careers). Comprehensive EisnerAmper benefits. Hybrid (up to 2 days/week at local office or client location). Preferred location: Baton Rouge, LA. Ability to travel and work extended hours as needed.

item.title: Senior Policy Analyst – HRSA Cooperative Agreement (Term, Grant-Funded)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/23/2026.

Note: Grant-funded term position with anticipated end date October 31, 2027; continuation depends on grant renewal. Project completion bonus of $7,500–$10,000 available at end of term. Salary $112,000–$120,000. Hybrid in Washington, DC (2 days in-office/3 days remote per week). 4–5 years of applied work experience required (master’s in political science, public policy, public health, or related field can substitute for 2 years). Experience managing federal grants or cooperative agreements a plus. Apply by completing the online form with resume and cover letter (link in posting). No phone calls.

The National Association of Medicaid Directors (NAMD) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit professional association representing leaders of state Medicaid agencies and Children’s Health Insurance Programs (CHIP) across all 56 states and territories. NAMD seeks a Senior Policy Analyst to manage the association’s HRSA-funded cooperative agreement, which aims to build literacy among state and territory Medicaid directors and public health leaders about HRSA priorities and initiatives, establish strong routine connections between Medicaid Directors and state/territory public health leaders, and identify opportunities to align strategies and braid use of HRSA and Medicaid funding. Hybrid, Washington, DC. Salary $112,000–$120,000.

Key responsibilities include: serving as project manager across NAMD’s state programming, federal policy, communications, and operations teams; liaising directly with state/territory Medicaid and public health leaders, HRSA, national associations, and other external partners for the purpose of creating connection between Medicaid and public health; coordinating strategic meetings with NAMD leadership, state/territory Medicaid leaders, HRSA leadership, public health officials, behavioral health officials, community health centers, and other external partners; identifying and coordinating opportunities for HRSA engagement with state/territory Medicaid leaders at NAMD’s Fall Conference, Annual Membership Meeting, and other events; designing and convening virtual events with state/territory Medicaid leaders and public health leaders to support shared learning; developing written resources to translate policy issues into actionable materials; coordinating collection and analysis of information from Medicaid leaders through polls, surveys, and listservs; and leading performance measurement, reporting, and evaluation efforts for NAMD’s HRSA cooperative agreement.

Qualifications: at least 4–5 years of applied work experience in public policy, public health, government, or related areas with some applied work experience in health policy (master’s in political science, public policy, public health, or related area can substitute for 2 years); demonstrated project and grant management skills (experience managing federal grants or cooperative agreements a plus); excellent written and oral communication skills; ability to manage multiple competing tasks and self-direct workflow; and excellent interpersonal skills. Lived experience with the Medicaid program is greatly valued.

Compensation and logistics: salary $112,000–$120,000 plus project completion bonus of $7,500–$10,000. Comprehensive NAMD benefits including 401(k) with up to 5% employer match after six months plus 5% discretionary after one year (vested from day one), medical/dental/vision, life insurance, STD/LTD, monthly cellular reimbursement, annual professional development stipend, and generous vacation and leave. Hybrid in Washington, DC (2 days in-office/3 days remote). Grant-funded through October 31, 2027. Apply via the online form with resume and cover letter. No phone calls.

item.description:

Apply via USAJOBS (search CRS Research Assistant Domestic Social Policy). Salary at CRS/LOC pay scale (confirm via USAJOBS/CRS). U.S. citizenship required. The Congressional Research Service is a nonpartisan legislative branch agency.

The Congressional Research Service (CRS) Domestic Social Policy (DSP) Division seeks a Research Assistant (RA) to provide research support tasks across a broad range of domestic policy and social program issues. CRS is the nonpartisan research arm of Congress, providing authoritative, objective, and confidential research and analysis to Members of Congress and their staff. Issue areas covered by this position include: (1) Children and Families issues especially as related to low-income populations; (2) Domestic Security and Immigration including crime policy and border security; (3) Education and Labor including training and the workforce; (4) Health Insurance and Financing including Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, and private health insurance; (5) Health Services including the health care workforce and public health; and (6) Income Security including Social Security, pensions, disability, and unemployment.

Key responsibilities include: providing research support tasks across a broad range of domestic policy and social program issues including children and families, domestic security and immigration, education and labor, health insurance and financing, health services, and income security; supporting CRS analysts in preparing legislative research, analysis, and consultation products; conducting literature searches and compiling background materials; and assisting with the production of CRS products for congressional audiences.

Qualifications: apply via USAJOBS for specific qualification requirements (search CRS Research Assistant Domestic Social Policy). U.S. citizenship required. The Congressional Research Service is a nonpartisan legislative branch agency with high standards for nonpartisan, objective research.

Compensation and logistics: salary at CRS/LOC pay scale (confirm via USAJOBS/CRS). Comprehensive Library of Congress federal benefits. Washington, DC. Nonpartisan legislative branch agency. Apply via USAJOBS.

item.title: White House Fellows Program – 2027–2028 Class
item.description:
Note: Application deadline January 14, 2027 (letters of recommendation due January 21, 2027). Submit application via whitehousefellows.gov using Login.gov. U.S. citizenship required. Undergraduate degree completion required by application deadline (graduate degree not required). Most federal employees are not eligible (exceptions: career military personnel and some special government employees). No age restriction. Active-duty military applicants must obtain required permission. TS/SCI clearance eligibility required (dual citizens may apply). Fellows receive a competitive federal salary during the program year. Washington, DC (year-long, full-time commitment).

The White House Fellows Program is one of America’s most prestigious programs for leadership and public service. Founded in 1964, the program has a nonpartisan tradition and has operated under both Republican and Democratic administrations. White House Fellows are selected by the President’s Commission on White House Fellowships to serve for one year in paid federal service working with a senior government principal, with an educational program complementing the placement through discussions with leaders and study of public policy in practice. Applications for the 2027–2028 class are open. Application deadline January 14, 2027.

The selection process is competitive. Former Fellows screen applications to identify the most promising candidates, and the most qualified applicants are selected to be interviewed by regional panels. Approximately 30 candidates proceed as National Finalists; the President’s Commission then interviews and recommends 11–19 outstanding candidates for a one-year presidential appointment. National Finalists are subject to investigation and verification by accredited federal investigators. Fellows must be eligible to obtain a top-secret security clearance.

The application consists of three parts: Part 1 (personal information, contact details, eligibility information, current employment, declarations); Part 2 (education, employment, and civic/volunteer experience; six essays covering current employment (200 words), most significant professional achievement (200 words), most significant community service achievement (200 words), lifetime goals (300 words), motivation for becoming a White House Fellow (300 words), and a 500-word memorandum for the President); and Part 3 (three letters of recommendation, with an optional fourth). Fellows receive a competitive federal salary, are eligible for Federal Employee Health Benefits, and are responsible for their own housing arrangements in Washington, DC. All activities are mandatory; the program year is a full-time commitment. Fellows may not receive outside salary or hold positions in outside organizations during the fellowship year.

Compensation and logistics: competitive federal salary. Federal Employee Health Benefit Plans available through placement agency. Washington, DC (year-long, full-time, mandatory commitment). U.S. citizenship required. Undergraduate degree required by application deadline. Must be eligible for TS/SCI clearance. Application deadline January 14, 2027. Apply at whitehousefellows.gov.

The HHS Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE) has fellowship opportunities available in the Office of Science and Data Policy. ASPE advises the HHS Secretary on policy development, leads special initiatives, coordinates the Department’s evaluation, research, and demonstration activities, and manages cross-Department planning activities. The selected fellow will be mentored by a team of economic, policy, and public health experts focusing on healthcare markets, with opportunities to train on a wide range of data resources, collaborate on research studies, and engage in quantitative and qualitative analytical projects supporting ASPE priorities. Washington, DC.

Learning objectives include: developing and maintaining subject matter expertise in rural healthcare systems, Medicaid policy, and Health Insurance Marketplace financing and eligibility frameworks; analyzing regulations, legislation, executive directives, and policy reports; conducting and supporting research and program evaluation activities; synthesizing complex policy information into clear, actionable insights; drafting professional correspondence, policy briefs, reports, presentations, and talking points; and communicating policy analysis and research findings in support of strategic briefings for HHS leadership.

Qualifications: master’s or doctoral degree in economics or a related field received within the past five years; experience designing, planning, conducting, and communicating the results of analytical projects; and knowledge of and experience with methodological and statistical techniques for analyzing and interpreting relevant data.

Compensation and logistics: monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience, plus a healthcare stipend. Washington, DC. ORISE fellowship (not federal employment). U.S. citizens and LPRs only. Appointment initially for one year, may be renewed. Application deadline: December 1, 2026 at 3:00 PM ET.

item.company: Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies (APAICS)
item.title: Congressional Fellowship 2027-2028
item.description:
Application deadline: December 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. A completed application must include: a cover letter expressing interest in the program; a one-page maximum resume; an academic transcript; two letters of recommendation (submitted by recommenders directly via the APAICS portal by December 18); and responses to three written questions (each no more than one page, double-spaced, 12-point Times New Roman font).

Note: APAICS Congressional Fellows are not employees of the federal government, their host office, or APAICS. Fellows receive a monthly educational stipend. Program dates: August 30, 2027–August 25, 2028. Washington, DC. This fellowship has a focus on Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander (AAPI) communities and public policy.

The Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies (APAICS) Congressional Fellowship offers individuals the opportunity to serve our nation and deepen their understanding of public policy through participation in the legislative process. Fellows are placed with a congressional office or committee for 12 months and are given work equivalent to that of a congressional legislative aide. By the end of the fellowship, fellows will have established a professional network on Capitol Hill, understand how Congress operates, and acquired skills and expertise that make them marketable to congressional offices, federal agencies, nonprofits, and the private sector.

Each fellowship experience will differ depending on the office in which fellows are placed and the portfolio assigned; however, fellows gather as a cohort twice a month to discuss their experiences and for professional development opportunities. Fellows are also expected to attend APAICS-organized events including the Annual Awards Gala and policy summits, and must make a public presentation on a policy topic of their choosing toward the end of the fellowship year.

The three written questions ask applicants to: (1) describe how they envision the APAICS fellowship playing a role in their career path and what they hope to gain; (2) describe their experience in the U.S. with AAPI communities and how proximity to or distance from these communities has shaped their views on public policy; and (3) describe a time when they worked as part of a team and encountered a challenge.

Compensation and logistics: monthly educational stipend (amount not stated; confirm via APAICS). 12-month fellowship. Washington, DC. Program dates: August 30, 2027–August 25, 2028. Application deadline: December 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.

item.title: Postgraduate Fellowship 2027-2028
item.description:
Application deadline: December 1, 2026. Apply via the CHCI website at chci.org.

Note: This is a paid, 9-month fellowship. A master's degree or JD completed within two years of the August 2027 program start date is required (i.e., degree completed after approximately August 2025). Program dates: August 18, 2027–May 19, 2028. Washington, DC. This fellowship is designed for emerging Latino leaders and individuals deeply committed to the Latino community.

The Congressional Hispanic Caucus Institute (CHCI) Postgraduate Fellowship Program offers emerging Latino leaders and individuals deeply committed to the Latino community the opportunity to draw connections between their graduate field of study and public policy. This paid, nine-month fellowship allows fellows to spend four days per week on Capitol Hill obtaining unparalleled work experience and exposure to the legislative process, and one day per week in leadership development programming centered on CHCI's four Pillars of Leadership. Fellows also organize and host a Capitol Hill briefing on a policy topic and publish an issue brief with CHCI.

Available fellowship concentrations include: Child Welfare, Health, Housing, Education, Law, Technology, and Transportation.

Program requirements include: working a minimum of 32 hours per week at a placement site; attending a 9-day orientation and weekly leadership development sessions throughout the program; completing community service hours; participating in all CHCI-sponsored activities including Hispanic Heritage Month events, summits, and receptions; researching, writing, and publishing an issue brief on a topic that impacts the Latino community within the fellowship discipline; planning, developing, and executing a policy briefing on Capitol Hill; and complying with CHCI policies regarding work performance and personal conduct.

Qualifications: a master's degree in any field or JD completed within two years of the August 2027 program start date.

Compensation and logistics: paid fellowship (stipend amount not stated; confirm via chci.org). 9-month program, August 18, 2027–May 19, 2028. Four days/week Capitol Hill placement; one day/week leadership development. Washington, DC. Application deadline: December 1, 2026.

item.title: Health Policy Fellowship (ORISE)
item.description:
A fellowship opportunity is available in the Office of Health Policy within the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE) at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in Washington, DC. Note: this is an ORISE-administered fellowship (administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy). Participants do not become employees of HHS, DOE, or the program administrator -- this is a stipend, not a salary, and there are no employment-related benefits. U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required. A master's or doctoral degree received within the past 5 years is required. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis; final deadline December 1, 2026.

The selected fellow will be mentored by a team of economic, policy, and public health experts who focus on healthcare markets, and will have opportunities to train with a wide range of data resources, collaborate on research studies, and engage in both quantitative and qualitative analytical projects in support of ASPE's priorities. Learning objectives include: developing and maintaining subject matter expertise in rural healthcare systems, Medicaid policy, and Health Insurance Marketplace financing and eligibility frameworks; analyzing regulations, legislation, executive directives, and policy reports; conducting and supporting research and program evaluation activities; synthesizing complex policy information into clear, actionable insights; and drafting professional correspondence, policy briefs, reports, presentations, and talking points.

Qualifications: a master's or doctoral degree in a relevant field (social science or related) received within the past five years; experience designing, planning, conducting, and communicating the results of analytical projects within economics or related fields; and knowledge of and experience with methodological and statistical techniques. The office has particular interest in applicants with experience in demography or actuarial science (not required). U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required.

Compensation and logistics: monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience; stipend for healthcare benefits (not employer-sponsored benefits). One-year initial appointment, may be renewed contingent on funding. Full-time. Based in Washington, DC. Application deadline: December 1, 2026 (rolling reviews).
